doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

chapter: James Taylor band and big band
title: Pandemic big band and playing with peers
summary: Marini wrote 13 big band pieces during the pandemic, recorded them with young monsters on sax, and values peer approval, including in James Taylor's band.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well I feel that all the time. During the pandemic I had a burst of creativity and I recorded — I mean I wrote 13 new big band compositions and in February I recorded them with a big band that I’ve been rehearsing. And there are, in the saxophone section, the baritone player is Dave Rickenberg. He plays his ass off. He’s in his 50s I suppose. There’s two young saxophone players, an alto player named Andrew Gold and a tenor player named Sam Dillon, and they are monsters. And Lawrence Waldron is the lead alto player. He and I played on Saturday Night Live together and we’ve been playing together for years and years. He’s a few years younger than me. And then the other tenor player is a guy named Matt Hong who went to North Texas and he’s in his 40s, and he’s a monster. So, and during the course of rehearsing with this band I had, you know, you could never get the same band twice in a row so you’re always having to hire subs, and
just in the saxophone section we heard like a dozen young saxophone players all of whom just make you want to jump in the practice room and try to — yeah.
I bet they were thrilled to be there too.

Yeah. Well that’s sort of a nice thing. You know we’re playing for our peers basically and their approval, and a glance of approval from one of them after a solo means more than anything else you can get you know, so — I mean you know playing with James Taylor’s band night to night, Larry Goldings, Michael Landau, Steve Gadd, Jimmy Johnson, Walt Fowler, you know, you pinch yourself you know. It’s like some honor to be playing with them you know.
